newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 2.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 2.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING:

WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton asks the Federal Communications Commission to study ways to curb television liquor ads following the industry's decision to abandon its nearly half-century voluntary ban.

CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp is taking on its main competitor Burger King in a television advertising campaign to promote its french fries. "We consider our fries to be the gold standard in the industry," a McDonald's spokeswoman says. "No one can match them."

ST. LOUIS, Missouri - Trans World Airlines is launching a print, radio and television advertising campaign in the New York market. "TWA has refocused its operation in the New York area to improve customer service and to concentrate on those destinations New Yorkers want most," says a spokeswoman.

PHOENIX, Arizona - The tobacco industry manipulated nicotine levels and courted underage smokers despite knowing for years that its product was toxic, according to tobacco industry documents. The Arizona Republic, citing confidential internal documents, said Liggett Group weighed using a synthetic substance in its products because of the "severe toxicity of nicotine."
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:

LONDON - Britain's newest terrestrial television station Channel 5 is likely to win more of its audience from Channel 4 and BBC2 than from the mainstream BBC1 and ITV channels, a report from Zenith Media, the media-buying and planning arm of Cordiant Plc, says.

LONDON - Johnston Press Plc, one of Britain's leading regional newspaper groups, says trading conditions have improved for its core business and that the outlook is encouraging. "Both advertising volumes and revenues are currently more encouraging in many areas and reflect the stronger performance of the national economy," says a spokesman.

PARIS - Television par Satellite has signed up 105,000 subscribers and should have 300,000 by the end of the year, 50,000 more than its initial goal, president Patrick Le Lay says. In an interview on French television LCI, he said the 2.5 billion francs ($444.7 million) earmarked for the new digital satellite television system by its founders should enable it to reach a million subscribers in four years.
CHICAGO - First Chicago NBD Corp, the ninth largest bank in the U.S., says it plans in 1997 to open a "virtual bank" on the Internet as more and more of its customers are choosing to bank online.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:

BUDAPEST - Volkswagen AG hung onto a narrow lead in January over Fiat SPA in central Europe's booming market for new autos, according to a monthly Reuters survey. VW outsold its Italian rival 14,797 units to 14,408 units in the Central European Free Trade Agreement countries -- the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.

BEIJING - Shenzhen Lionda Holdings Co Ltd plans to take part in a $50 million amusement part project in the central China city of Wuhan, Wuhan mayor Wang Shouhai says. Construction would start in May and would be completed in two years, Wang says.

BEIJING - Troubled Sino-French car venture Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile has lowered the price of its spare parts by an average of 20 percent, a company official says. The price cuts follow complaints from car owners that spares and repairs were too expensive.
MEXICO CITY - Mexico City opens its doors to long-distance telephone competition, officially ending Telefonos de Mexico's decades-old grip on the sprawling metropolis.
SINGAPORE - Paging firm Sunpage launches its messaging operations with low prices aimed at taking a third of the newly deregulated Singapore market.

LONDON - Sony Computer Entertainment, a unit of Sony Corp, says it sold 50,000 units of its PlayStation game machine in the UK in the week March 22-29, making it the largest single week's sales of any console since Christmas 1996.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

SINGAPORE- The chip, Britain's best known contribution to world cuisine, is alive and well and coming to Asia. No longer wrapped in vinegar-sodden newspaper, the deep fried slice of potato has been repackaged for the 1990s and "branded" for maximum marketing mileage, says fish and chip restaurant chain Harry Ramsden's.
LONDON - Pub group J.D. Wetherspoon Plc is to take advantage of increased interest in pub-going by opening 350 new pubs in the next five years, it says.

BEIJING - China's rail system enters the marketplace as trains start to run faster to try to win back passengers who have switched to buses and planes for speed and comfort. China's trains carried only 942 million passengers last year, a 12.3 percent drop from the previous year while air travel boomed.
